title: Fibrewise injectivity criterion for a flat finitely presented module
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $\Sigma\subseteq B$ be a multiplicative subset (containing $1$ and closed under multiplication), and put $C=\Sigma^{-1}B$, the ring of fractions $b/s$ with the usual localization equivalence. Let $N$ be a finitely presented $C$-module, meaning the cokernel of a map $C^r\to C^q$ with $r,q$ finite, and suppose $N$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $M$ be any flat $A$-module and let $u:N\to M$ be $A$-linear; no $B$-module structure on $M$ is required. If $u\otimes_A\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}$ is injective for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, then $u\otimes_A\mathrm{id}_Q:N\otimes_AQ\to M\otimes_AQ$ is injective for every $A$-module $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the fraction field of $A/\mathfrak p$; $A,B,N,M$ need not be Noetherian or finite as $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 0AT9, lemma-universally-injective-if-flat, with its situation equation-star

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-target-ideal-quotient-injectivity-test], it suffices to prove injectivity modulo each finitely generated ideal $J\subseteq A$. Fix $J$ and replace $(A,B,C,N,M,u)$ by $(A/J,B/JB,C/JC,N/JN,M/JM,\bar u)$. These objects again satisfy all hypotheses: substitute the images of the coefficients in the finite algebra presentation and module presentation, and use $(\Sigma^{-1}B)\otimes_AA/J\cong\bar\Sigma^{-1}(B/JB)$. This identification sends $(b/s)\otimes\bar a$ to $\bar a\bar b/\bar s$, with inverse $\bar b/\bar s\mapsto(b/s)\otimes1$. Both modules are flat over $A/J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. A prime of $A/J$ is a prime of $A$ containing $J$, with the same residue field, so its fibre map is precisely the original fibre map. Thus it suffices to prove ordinary injectivity for arbitrary data satisfying the original hypotheses; the remaining steps prove this assertion without assuming any of the quotient maps injective.

source.place: Tag 0AT9, first paragraph; equation-star base change paragraph

proof.text: Suppose $0\ne x\in\ker u$. The ideal $H=\operatorname{Ann}_A(x)=\{a:ax=0\}$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] choose a prime $\mathfrak p$ minimal over $H$. In the cyclic module $Ax$ it is weakly associated, in the explicit sense of clause (1) of [lem-sc-weakass-localization]. Clause (3) supplies a nonzero element $y\in(Ax)_{\mathfrak p}$ whose annihilator has radical $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. View it inside $N_{\mathfrak p}$: localization preserves the inclusion, directly because a fraction is zero exactly when some denominator kills its numerator. Also $u_{\mathfrak p}(y)=0$. Replace the data by their base changes to $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and rename this local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$. Finite presentations and the residue-field hypothesis persist by the same substitutions as in step 1, and flatness persists by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. We now have $0\ne y\in\ker u$ and $\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}_A(y)}=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0AT9, second paragraph, weakly associated prime localization (Tags 0588 and 0566)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-finite-presentation-pure-spreadout] to this local base, obtaining $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $P$ projective over $R=A/I$, and a universally injective localization map $j:P\to\bar N=N/IN$. Put $\bar M=M/IM$, flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. For each $s\in\Sigma$, consider $v_s:P\xrightarrow{j}\bar N\xrightarrow{1/s}\bar N\xrightarrow{\bar u}\bar M$. Reduction modulo the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$ is injective: $j$ remains injective by its universal injectivity, $1/s$ is an automorphism, and the reduction of $\bar u$ is the assumed fibre injection at $\mathfrak m$. The local projective-source criterion [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] therefore makes every $v_s$ universally injective over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0AT9, choice of I; Tag 0AT7, lemma-properties-pure-spreadout part (2), projective-source argument

proof.text: For every $R$-module $T$, each element $z\in\bar N\otimes_RT$ is the image of some $w\in P\otimes_RT$ under $(1/s)j\otimes1_T$ for a single $s\in\Sigma$. Indeed write $z$ as a finite sum of pure tensors, express each first factor as $j(p_i)/s_i$, and take the product of the denominators; multiplying $p_i$ by the other denominators puts every summand over that product. This uses the localization isomorphism provided by [lem-sfb-local-finite-presentation-pure-spreadout] and tensor generation and bilinearity from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $(\bar u\otimes1_T)(z)=0$, then $(v_s\otimes1_T)(w)=0$, so step 3 gives $w=0$ and $z=0$. Thus $\bar u$ is universally injective over $R$. Equivalently $u\otimes1_T$ is injective for every $A$-module $T$ annihilated by $I$: the tensor relations over $A$ and over $A/I$ coincide after killing $IN$ and $IM$.

source.place: Tag 0AT7, part (2), final filtered-localization argument, with denominators written out

proof.text: Choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $I$. Since each belongs to $\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}(y)}$, choose positive integers $e_i$ with $a_i^{e_i}y=0$. Every monomial of degree $n=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$ in the generators contains such a power, so $I^ny=0$. If $r=0$, use $n=1$. Let $K=\operatorname{Ann}_A(I^n)$. This ideal has the finite filtration $K\supseteq IK\supseteq\cdots\supseteq I^nK=0$, each successive quotient annihilated by $I$. Step 4 gives injectivity after tensoring $u$ with each quotient. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to both $N$ and $M$ and each short exact sequence $0\to I^{j+1}K\to I^jK\to I^jK/I^{j+1}K\to0$. Descending induction on $j$, starting with $j=n$, proves that $u\otimes1_K$ is injective: a kernel element has zero image in the quotient tensor, hence lifts to the preceding submodule tensor, where injectivity and the injective inclusion into the target tensor force it to vanish.

source.place: Tag 0AT9, last paragraph, ideal-power reduction made explicit

proof.text: The ideal $I^n$ is finitely generated; list its degree-$n$ monomial generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$. The sequence $0\to K\to A\xrightarrow{a\mapsto(b_1a,\ldots,b_ta)}A^t$ is exact. Tensor with the flat module $N$ using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Under the bilinear identifications $N\otimes_AA=N$ and $N\otimes_AA^t=N^t$, this identifies $N\otimes_AK$ with the submodule of elements killed by every $b_i$, namely $\operatorname{Ann}_N(I^n)$. Consequently $y$ lifts to a nonzero $z\in N\otimes_AK$. Tensoring $K\hookrightarrow A$ with $M$ is injective by the same cited lemma. The natural square for $u$ commutes, since both paths send $n\otimes k$ to $ku(n)$. As $u(y)=0$, it follows that $(u\otimes1_K)(z)=0$, contradicting step 5. Thus $u$ is injective. Step 1 applies this ordinary-injectivity argument over every $A/J$, and the quotient test then proves the required injectivity for every $Q$.
